2026-11-20.title: Friday after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
2026-11-20.verse: For, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
theo: Salvation is not far away, Paul says, as if we had to climb to heaven or descend to the abyss to fetch Christ. “The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart.” If you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. There is no distinction between Jew and Greek: the same Lord is generous to all who call on him.

Jesus tells of a sower who throws seed everywhere: on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns, and on good soil. The sower is not stingy; the seed is the same; the difference is the soil. Some hearts are hard as a path, some shallow, some choked with worries. But the good soil yields thirty, sixty, a hundredfold. Each day we choose what kind of soil we will be.
outline: What kind of soil am I today?
On your lips and in your heart.
“Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
live: Say “Jesus is Lord” aloud in your morning prayer.
Remove one distraction that chokes your prayer.
2026-11-20.prayer: Lord Jesus, your word is near us. Make our hearts good soil, clear away the thorns of worry, and let us call on your name and be saved. Amen.

quick: The word is near: on your lips and in your heart.
All who call on the Lord will be saved.
Be good soil for the seed.
2026-11-20.action: Remove one distraction that chokes your prayer.
2026-11-20.question: Which thorns choke the word in me?

homily: Dear friends, Paul says salvation is not far away, as if we had to climb to heaven or descend to the abyss to fetch Christ. The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart. If you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved (Romans 10:8–9). Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

In the parable of the sower the same seed falls on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns and on good soil; what fell on good soil brought forth grain, a hundredfold, sixtyfold, thirtyfold. Let anyone with ears listen (Matthew 13:3–9).

The word is near; the question is how open our heart is. This week let us call on the name of Jesus in our heart throughout the day: Lord Jesus, have mercy on me. That short prayer turns the heart into good soil. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus saves everyone who calls on his name. Today say many times in your heart: Jesus, I love you.

intro: Confess, call, and be good soil.
